# Spells still to fix

Every spell below still carries keys in `special.legacy`. A spell leaves this
document when that block is empty, so the counts are the progress bar.

The registry is `resources/data/spell_effects.json`; `validate_data.py` enforces
it. Migrating a spell means moving each legacy key into `special.effects` as a
typed entry and deleting it from `legacy` **and** from the frozen list in the
registry — the frozen list may shrink and must never grow.

## The shape of the job

| Batch | Spells | What it needs |
|---|---:|---|
| A — mechanical | 0 | Every key routes to a type and already carries its value. No decisions. |
| B — filed in the wrong place | 0 | The fact is fine; it belongs on the summon template, the targeting block, or nowhere. |
| C — needs a number | 94 | The key names a real mechanic and was written as bare `true`. Someone picks the number. |
| D — needs a decision | 90 | No registry type fits. What should the spell actually do? |
| **total** | **184** | of 362 spells |

**Do them in that order.** A and B are mechanical and shrink the list fast; C is
far fewer decisions than it looks because the keys repeat — answer `freeze_chance`
once and eight spells migrate. D is the genuinely new design work and it is worth
asking, spell by spell, whether the spell needs the mechanic at all.

## Batch A — mechanical, no decisions needed

Every key here routes onto a registry type and already carries the value that type wants. These can be migrated in one pass without asking anyone anything.


## Batch B — the fact is right, the field is wrong

Nothing here needs inventing. These keys describe the summoned creature (which belongs on its entry in `summon_templates.json`), or the spell's range and shape (which `target` and `aoe` already model), or they restate the description in snake_case and carry nothing the engine could act on — those just go.


## Batch C — a real mechanic missing its number

The key names something the game could do; it was written as a bare `true`, so migrating it means choosing the number it never carried. Work the recurring-key table above first — most of these fall out of a handful of answers.

### What batch D is telling us

Reading the unrouted keys together, they are not 90 unrelated ideas. Four
clusters account for most of them, and each is one missing registry type:

1. **A trigger wrapper.** `triggers_on`, `triggers_when_ally_dies`,
   `when_target_dies`, `if_kills_chain_to_next_target`, `if_kills_raise_as_zombie`,
   `on_success`, `melee_counter_burn`, `breaks_on_offensive_action`,
   `consumed_on_hit`. The registry has no way to say *when* an effect fires. This
   is the single biggest gap and probably wants a `when` param on every effect
   rather than a type of its own.
2. **Damage typing.** `white_damage`, `adds_air_damage`, `damage_split`,
   `non_physical_damage_only`, `cannot_deal_physical`. Damage currently has no
   element attached to it at all. That is a combat-system decision, not a spell one.
3. **Shields and absorbs.** `hp_shield`, `physical_immunity`,
   `physical_negation_25_percent`, `spell_damage_reduction`,
   `ranged_damage_reduction`, `must_destroy_before_damage`. All want one
   `damage_reduction` or `shield` type with a source filter.
4. **Resurrection.** `resurrects_with_1hp`, `resurrects_with_full_hp`,
   `resurrects_all_fallen_allies`, `partial_hp_on_resurrect`, `rise_as_zombie`,
   `return_next_turn`, `return_with_20_percent_hp`. One `resurrect` type with an
   hp param covers every one.

The remainder are genuinely one-off and several should probably just be cut.


## Batch D — no registry type fits

These are the ones worth talking through. Some want a new effect type in the registry (`hp_shield`, `stops_time`, `resurrects_*`, the several `spreads_to_*` keys). Some describe a mechanic the game does not have and may not want. Some are one spell's private idea. For each: new effect type, existing type with a stretch, or cut it.
